correctness.rationale: For the five printed decimal rational coefficients treated exactly, Schur inequalities hold for every s>0. When s<=s0=c/d both A,B>=0; when s>=s1=a/b the second iterate is negative. On s0<s<s1, roots p>0 and -q<0 have q>p, and exact starting solution has coefficients (u+q)/(p+q), (p-u)/(p+q), u=e^-s. Every iterate is positive iff u=p, otherwise the dominant alternating mode eventually gives negative parity. Exact matching is F(s)=0. The derivative analysis of H=e^sF’’ with H’’>0 and explicit endpoint/interior signs bounds F to two simple zeros. Independent high-precision root calculations locate 3.70146585514664567398 and 46.340425531914893290594485997229844; the second is ~3.26e-16 below s1 and direct finite iteration there is ill-conditioned, so it was NOT used as a proof. Log ratio of amplitudes proves inverse-linear first-negative index near s0 and logarithmic delay near simple resonance. Bounded numerical checks support but do not replace the derivative sign proof.
